PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 18, audited at commit 3029f89 (HEAD of the main checkout, tree 3f53f123...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict, including the 23 Aug addition of R9 and R10 from GroundTruth's Sprint 17 finding. Six files, 312 insertions. VERDICT: PASS. Closing sprint of the epic, and the criterion it named as mattering most is met by construction rather than by care. R9 -- STORED XSS THROUGH THE HOROSCOPE COLUMN. MET, and met in the way that survives the next person. Grepped app/, lib/ and package.json for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, marked, markdown, remark, rehype, react-markdown and sanitize. Exactly one hit in the entire repository: a comment in app/reading/[id]/display.ts saying not to use them. package.json is untouched by this sprint, so no markdown library was added -- which is the specific vector the requirement named, and the tempting one, since the model's output really does arrive as "two to four short paragraphs" in one string. horoscopeParagraphs splits on /\n+/, trims, filters empties, and returns string[]; page.tsx maps each to

{paragraph}

. That is JSX text content, escaped by React, and the helper's own comment records why it must stay that way and where the untrusted content comes from -- anon-writable via set_reading_horoscope, Sprint 17 R3/R4. A requirement satisfied by a comment is a requirement waiting to regress; this one is satisfied by there being no HTML-interpreting path in the codebase at all. AND SOMETHING NOT ASKED FOR, which I want on the record because it is the same class of bug one field over. isSafeExternalUrl gates every event sourceUrl on startsWith ("https://") before it reaches an href, with tests rejecting a javascript: scheme. R9 did not mention it. It matters: React escapes text content but does not sanitise href, so a javascript: URL in an href is executable, and the events column is anon-writable on insert exactly as the horoscope column is on update -- an attacker can create their own reading carrying a crafted sourceUrl and share the link. The guard closes it. One correction to its comment, which is narrower than the threat it actually defends against: the comment says sourceUrl "comes from Wikipedia, not from the anon-writable horoscope column". It comes from the row, and the row's events column is anon-writable on insert under Sprint 4's with-check-true policy. The code is right; the reasoning under it understates why. THE THREE CARRIED FIXES, each correct: R5 MET. generate.ts's catch binds the error and console.errors it before returning the generic message. The swallow stays, as R8 of Sprint 17 requires; what changes is that a quota, rate-limit or billing failure now leaves a trace. R6 MET. saveReading console.errors the Supabase error before redirecting. Carried since Sprint 14, where fixing it would have been exactly the scope creep that sprint forbade. Closed in the sprint that scoped it. R7 MET, and met as a fallback rather than a catch -- which the criterion singled out as the point. assertDateInSupportedRange(later) is checked before computePositions(later) is ever called, and on failure computePromptAspects returns the caller's own composeChart aspects. The distinction is preserved exactly: the user gets a real answer, not "try again", which would have been misleading advice for a date that will never work. I verified the fix the same way I found the bug -- by running it, not by reading the test. At Sprint 17's HEAD, generateAndPersistHoroscope for a 2100-12-31 reading threw past its caller. At this commit it returns { ok: true }. And there is now a regression test at exactly that level, plus a unit test asserting the fallback identity, so it cannot come back quietly. Requirements coverage: R1 MET. Positions, aspects, balance and moon phase from composeChart; events; and the horoscope. This is also where Sprint 12's aspect engine -- tested and unused since Sprint 14's revert -- finally gets a caller, which is the outcome Sprint 14's R8 argued for when it justified keeping the code. R2 MET. eventsLabel reads matchedYear off the stored payload. It is never inferred, and the false case reads as the normal case rather than as an error, which is right: with 23 entries spanning ~900 years the fallback is what usually happens. R3 MET. The control reads "Regenerate horoscope" when one exists and "Generate horoscope" when it does not, overwriting in place. R4 MET, every combination explicitly. events null -> the label says nothing was looked up and no list renders; horoscope null -> "No horoscope generated yet."; no aspects within orb -> "No aspects within orb." Nothing renders as an empty region. R8 MET. Thirteen new display tests plus the two R7 tests: the three label states, four paragraph-splitting cases including single-newline and empty-line handling, four isSafeExternalUrl cases including the javascript: rejection, the fallback identity, and the end-to-end 2100-12-31 path returning a result. R9 MET. See above. R10 MET. Grepped the whole diff for className, style=, .css, oklch and styled: zero hits. No design pass happened by accident, on the sprint where the page finally has real content to style -- which is the sprint where it was most likely to. No schema change: git diff over supabase/ is empty and the migration count is 8 at both c3bf6fa and HEAD. Verified by execution: - lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 162 tests across 16 files, 13 new. - next build exits 0; route table unchanged. - Built with OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set to probe values and grepped the entire .next output: both absent. - The 2100-12-31 re-probe above. Notes, not conditions: 1. The R7 fallback restores Sprint 17's original defect for exactly one date. When it fires, the prompt gets composeChart's aspects, whose applying is structurally false, so a 2100-12-31 reading's prompt tells the model every aspect is separating -- the thing Sprint 17 round 1 was about. It is one date, the alternative was a framework error page, and a real answer beats a crash. A backward snapshot (t - 1 day, with the comparison inverted: applying when the orb was larger before) would give a correct answer at the top of the range too. Not worth requiring for a single boundary date; worth knowing the fallback is a downgrade rather than a neutral path. 2. The aspects table on the page deliberately omits applying/separating, and the comment says why: this page uses composeChart directly and has no reason to recompute a second snapshot, so showing nothing beats showing a label that would be wrong. That is the right call and I want it credited -- it is the same reasoning that made Sprint 17 round 1 a condition, applied by the team without being asked. 3. set_reading_horoscope's anon grant is explicitly out of scope here, correctly, and the sprint file records it as a decision rather than an omission. Restating the consequence once, since this is the last static gate of the epic: the stored horoscope is attacker-controllable for any shared link, R9 is what makes that safe to render, and R9 is the requirement most likely to be undone by a future sprint reaching for a markdown renderer. If anything in this epic deserves a standing note in README or CLAUDE.md rather than only in a closed sprint file, it is that. 4. Carried and unchanged: readingId is still interpolated unencoded into the redirect path (checked again -- cannot escape the origin, so not an open redirect), and the page still reflects searchParams.error as escaped text. Cleared to ship at 3029f89. GroundTruth's third criterion is the one this whole proof of concept was for -- three independent sources, synthesised, visible in one place, verified from outside the system -- and its second is the one that has silently verified every migration in this epic: the Sprint 14 fixture, with events and horoscope both null, still opening and rendering sensibly. R4 is what makes that work, and it is the requirement I would check first if that fixture ever stops rendering.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 18, round 2. Audited at commit ffce120, HEAD of the main checkout, recorded tree 0a230681... Sprint file re-read fresh; it has changed, which is why there is a round 2. Scope: README.md only, 26 insertions, 5 deletions. git diff --name-only 3029f89..HEAD returns README.md and nothing else, so all code is byte-identical to what I passed in round 1. VERDICT: PASS. WHAT CHANGED. Round 1's note 3 was promoted to R11 with its own acceptance criterion: R9's protection was enforced by a sprint file and one code comment, both of which close when the epic does, so the constraint needed a home that outlives them. That is the right call and the right place. Round 1's PASS stands unchanged -- the code did not move, the spec grew, and the hash check caught it, which is the mechanism working. R11 MET, all three points, and the third is the one I would have checked hardest: 1. Untrusted content, with the reason rather than just the assertion -- readings.events and readings.horoscope are anon-writable, set_reading_horoscope is granted to anon the same way insert is, and there is no owner concept to check against (Sprint 4). It tells a reader to treat both at the same trust level as any other public form submission, which is the correct mental model rather than a rule to memorise. 2. Escaped text only -- never dangerouslySetInnerHTML, never a markdown renderer permitting raw HTML, never innerHTML -- and, crucially, it names the technique that makes the safe path also the convenient one: split on newlines, map each to a

as JSX text content, no markdown library needed at all. It then says outright that reaching for one to get the same paragraph rendering is what turns a shared link into stored XSS. That sentence is the whole point of the note. Someone will want paragraphs; this tells them how to have them safely before they go looking. 3. The sourceUrl scheme check, framed exactly as the criterion demanded -- "a separate guard from escaping, not a redundant one", because React's escaping protects text content and does nothing about a javascript: URL sitting in an attribute. A note covering only escaping would have been the likely outcome here and would have left the href path undefended in the documentation while it stayed defended in the code. It does not. Re-verified rather than assumed, since a documentation change is exactly where it would be easy to describe a guard that no longer exists: - isSafeExternalUrl is still exported from display.ts and still gates event.sourceUrl at page.tsx:131 before it reaches an href. - Re-grepped app/, lib/ and package.json for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, react-markdown, remark, rehype and "marked": one hit, the same comment in display.ts telling people not to. No markdown dependency was added. - lint, typecheck, test all exit 0. 162 tests across 16 files, unchanged from round 1 as expected for a README-only commit. Round 1's coverage of R1 through R10 stands in full and I am not restating it; the tree is identical apart from README. Notes, not conditions: 1. One imprecision in the new note, worth correcting whenever README is next open. It says both columns are "anon-writable by anyone holding a reading id". That is exact for horoscope -- set_reading_horoscope takes the id and there is no other write path. For events it is narrower than the truth: an anon does not need anyone's reading id, they insert their own row under Sprint 4's with-check-true insert policy and put whatever they like in events, then share that link. The operative instruction is unaffected, since both are untrusted either way, but a standing security note is exactly the document where someone might later reason "events only comes from our own saveReading" and relax the guard. "Anon-writable" without the qualifier would be both shorter and more accurate. 2. Related and carried from round 1: display.ts's own comment on isSafeExternalUrl still says sourceUrl "comes from Wikipedia, not from the anon-writable horoscope column", which is the same understatement. The README is now the authoritative version and it is closer to right; the code comment is the narrow one. Worth reconciling them so they do not drift further apart, since they defend the same line of code. 3. Carried and unchanged: readingId is still interpolated unencoded into the redirect path (re-checked, still cannot escape the origin), and the page still reflects searchParams.error as escaped text. Cleared to ship at ffce120. This is the last static gate of the epic, and the thing I would want a future reader to take from this record is the shape of R11 itself: the protection that survived was not the code, which any refactor can undo, but the sentence in README explaining why the obvious convenience -- a markdown renderer for paragraphs -- is the exact vector. GroundTruth's criteria are unchanged from round 1.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 18, commit ffce1205cde413eb63a71d61cc810f5c234a0063. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~02:20-02:25Z. VERDICT: PASS. All four criteria verified, plus R9 -- the escaping requirement my own Sprint 17 finding produced -- tested by attack rather than by reading the diff. Deployed commit confirmed: /api/health/db reports {"sha":"ffce1205cde413eb63a71d61cc810f5c234a0063","short":"ffce120","isLocal":false}. CRITERION 1 -- a reading with all three sources shows chart, events and horoscope, and states whether the events are year-matched or day-of-year. PASS. I checked BOTH states rather than one, because the label is only honest if it distinguishes. Year-matched, /reading/c78ee91d-... (1986-03-31), events section reads verbatim: "These events happened on this exact date." followed by "1986 : Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940 crashed into the Sierra Madre Oriental near Maravatío, killing 167 people. ( source )" Day-of-year fallback, /reading/d8407973-... (1977-03-31), events section reads verbatim: "No recorded event matched this exact year — showing notable happenings on this day across history instead." followed by 2023, 2018, ... entries, each with a source link. Two different sentences for two different states, and the fallback one says plainly that it is a fallback. R2 asked for the flag to be surfaced honestly and it is. Both pages render the chart, the events and the horoscope together. Sprint 12's engine is now visible too -- the fixture page shows element and modality counts and "Moon phase — Waxing gibbous". The code carried unused since Sprint 12, on the argument that deleting tested working code to re-derive it later was the worse trade, is now on screen. That argument is settled. CRITERION 2 -- the Sprint 14 fixture, with events and horoscope both null, still opens and renders sensibly rather than erroring. PASS. /reading/f8d046f7-6432-4961-b996-d65c9f623a8e -> 200, full chart rendered, and the two empty sections say what they are, verbatim: "Events | No events looked up for this reading." "Horoscope | No horoscope generated yet." with a Generate horoscope control. No error text anywhere on the page. A reading created eight sprints before either feature existed renders as a complete page, not a broken one. CRITERION 3 -- regenerating produces different prose and persists it. PASS. This is the sprint's actual proof. On /reading/c78ee91d-..., which carries all three sources: before len 1677, at 01:31:34Z, opens "On this fateful day, March 31, 1986, the cosmos painted a vibrant tapestry of ce..." regenerate 1 3370ms, len 1686, at 02:22:37Z, opens "On this fateful day, March 31, 1986, the fiery energy of Aries from the Sun and ..." regenerate 2 3355ms, len 1596, at 02:22:40Z, opens "On this fateful day, March 31, 1986, the cosmos was ablaze with the fiery energy..." All three texts distinct. Each regeneration overwrote in place -- one horoscope column, timestamp advancing, no accumulation. A cold page load afterwards renders the latest text and the superseded text is gone from the page. Three independent sources synthesised and visible in one place, verified from outside the system by a client holding nothing but a link and the public anon key. That is what the proof of concept was for. CRITERION 4 -- a reading for 2100-12-31 generates without a framework error page. PASS. This is Sprint 17's carried crash (R7), where computePromptAspects pushed a day past MAX_SUPPORTED_DATE and threw past the caller. Saved a reading for 2100-12-31 -> /reading/f8a6de6c-ce3e-4f3a-885f-2898b4f674fb Generate -> HTTP/2 303 back to the reading, 4691ms. Not an error redirect, not a crash: 4691ms is squarely in the range of a real OpenAI call. The rendered page: 200, chart rendered, horoscope present, and zero occurrences of "application error", "client-side exception", "Internal Server Error" or "Digest:" -- the markers a Next.js framework error page carries. The upper boundary of the supported range now generates like any other date. R9 -- THE HOROSCOPE COLUMN IS RENDERED ESCAPED. PASS, and I tested it the way the requirement was earned: by writing markup into the column and seeing what the page did with it, not by reading the component. Using only the public anon key, via set_reading_horoscope, I wrote this into a reading's horoscope (rpc -> 200): bold [link](javascript:alert(1)) Then fetched the page.
